agency: California Department of Health Care Services
applies_to: Adults ages 19 to 64 who get Medi-Cal because of their income, starting January 1, 2027. Medi-Cal will send you a letter if this applies to you, and your county Medi-Cal office will tell you if you need to follow the work rules.

ways_to_meet.text: Work at a job and earn at least $580 a month.
Be a seasonal worker and earn an average of $580 a month over the last six months.
Be in a job training program for at least 80 hours a month.
Volunteer or do community service for at least 80 hours a month.
Go to school at least half-time (usually two or three classes, or about six to eight credits each semester).
Do a mix of these so the total is at least 80 hours a month or at least $580 a month.

exemptions.question: Are you pregnant, or were you pregnant in the last year?
Are you a parent or caregiver of a child age 13 or younger?
Do you have a serious physical or mental health condition, or a substance use problem?
Were you released from jail or prison in the last 90 days?
Are you on Medicare Part A or Part B?
Are you American Indian or Alaska Native?
Are you under 26, and were you in foster care on your 18th birthday?
